$comment_schema: scripts/opencode/tool-arg-map.json — checked-in derived artifact.
fw-adr-0031 'Tool-name / arg-key mapping ownership' (binding): the
Claude tool <-> OpenCode tool correspondence and per-key arg renames
are an EXPLICIT table, not an inferred camelCase<->snake_case
transform. OpenCode's own arg-key casing is not internally consistent
(filePath/oldString/newString/content/command are camelCase, but
task's subagent_type is already snake_case) so a blanket regex would
either mis-handle subagent_type or need its own exception list -- an
explicit table is the correct shape, not an accident of convenience.
Read by BOTH .opencode/plugin/hook-bridge.js (payload construction)
and scripts/verify-opencode-hook-parity.sh (release-gate parity
check) -- the two must never see a different mapping.
Shape:
tools.<opencode_tool_id>.claude_tool_name  -- the Claude tool name
scripts/hooks/*.py expect in the 'tool_name' field of the
{tool_name, tool_input} payload (matches .claude/settings.json
PreToolUse matchers).
tools.<opencode_tool_id>.arg_map           -- { <opencode arg key>:
<claude tool_input key> }. The bridge copies
args[opencode_key] -> tool_input[claude_key] for every entry
present on the call; keys absent from the OpenCode call are
simply omitted (matches how a Claude tool_input can be sparse).
unmapped_claude_tools.<ClaudeToolName>     -- Claude tools guarded
by .claude/settings.json that have NO OpenCode source tool to
wire. Recorded explicitly (not silently absent) so
verify-opencode-hook-parity.sh can tell 'known gap, already
accounted for' apart from 'nobody updated the table'.
Runtime grounding: OpenCode 1.18.4, confirmed by a live runtime spike
(session probe under /tmp/ocspike at implementation time; see
FW-ADR-0031, recorded in the meta-project, not shipped with the
scaffold). The spike's callable
toolset was: bash, edit, glob, grep, invalid, question, read, skill,
task, todowrite, webfetch, websearch, write. There is NO 'patch' tool
in this version -- write and edit are the only file-mutation tools.

MultiEdit.reason: No OpenCode source tool. fw-adr-0031's Decision text anticipated an edit+patch split (OpenCode splits multi-hunk changes across edit and a unified-diff 'patch' tool) and required MultiEdit-matched hooks to be wired to both OpenCode tool ids. A runtime spike against the actually-installed OpenCode 1.18.4 (see opencode_version_verified above) found NO 'patch' tool in the callable toolset -- write and edit are the only file-mutation tools. MultiEdit-matched hooks (customer-notes-guard.py, tech-lead-authoring-guard.py, handoff-pre-tool-gate.py) are therefore covered for OpenCode purely via their write/edit wiring; there is no separate OpenCode tool call standing in for a Claude MultiEdit today. This entry exists so verify-opencode-hook-parity.sh can tell 'named, accepted gap' apart from 'someone forgot to map it'.
